context: Block-skill adjacency matrix data visualization showing which D3.js blocks use which skills, with zoom/pan, sort controls, and hover highlighting
first_impression: Intentional dark-theme design with a Nord-inspired categorical palette and satisfying hover interactions, but the auto-fit scale renders row labels too small to read without zooming in.
what_works: The hover interaction — dimming unrelated cells while highlighting the active row and column labels — is genuinely useful for a matrix this dense. The Nord-palette categorical colors against the dark background are a deliberate, harmonious choice well above default schemeCategory10.
what_doesnt: At the auto-fitted default scale, the 105 block-name labels on the left collapse to ~7-8px effective size, making them illegible without manual zoom — the matrix communicates pattern but not content at first render. The header bar is cramped, squeezing the title, two sort dropdowns, and seven legend items into one row with no visual breathing room.
